turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. Before the doctor calls you, bp is 128 over 82 and pulse is 76. I have put it on the slip.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ya, come, sit. Sorry, this computer is taking its own sweet time. What happened, tell me.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Uh, doctor, I twisted my ankle yesterday in the match. It is swollen and it is paining.
[SEG0004] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, he is my son. He plays cricket. Actually the ankle is paining from three days, he is limping only, he could not walk properly.
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): No papa. It was yesterday only, the right ankle, after the match, outer side. I can walk, it pains, but I came walking from the auto, maybe a small limp, I don't know.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. One second, the screen has frozen. Which ankle, say again?
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): Right one, doctor, outer side. I don't know how much swollen you will say, but the swelling is there.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): How it twisted, tell me once more, I was typing.
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): I play cricket. I was fielding, the ball came, my foot went inwards on the rough patch. Err, that is all.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any pop sound? And right now, can you take your full weight on it?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): Pop I don't know, doctor. I didn't notice. Weight I can take, it pains when I do.
[SEG0012] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And in the night he was having fever also. I touched the forehead, it was warm.
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): No papa. I didn't have fever. I don't know why you keep saying that.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. So somewhere between yesterday and three days, we will not argue the exact day. Any numbness in the toes?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Toes are fine.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the knee? Any pain up in the knee, or the other leg?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): No doctor. Only this ankle.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hmm, the old file is not opening. You are on any regular tablets? Tell me slowly.

[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): Umm, amlodipine for the pressure, in the morning. Then the cholesterol one at night, ten mg. Sugar tablets, metformine 500, morning and night. And only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): The pressure one, what mg? Say again, I missed it.
[SEG0021] person_1 (NURSE): Sir, in the previous note it is written amlodipine 5 mg once daily.
[SEG0022] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No no, sister, that is old. The physician changed it. He takes 10 mg every morning, ten only.
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. I just take whatever is in the box. I never read the mg.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ok. The cholesterol one, what is the name of that tablet?
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. White tablet, small, for the cholesterol, at night. Ten milligram, that much my mother told.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): And this Ayurvedic powder, which one is it?
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Some brown powder, one teaspoon, morning only. My mother mixes it in water.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright. Shoe off, let me look. Of. The light in here is poor also.

[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Swelling is there on the outer right ankle, and a little bluish bruise. I am pressing the back of the lateral malleolus, no tenderness on the bone. Medial malleolus, also I am not getting bony tenderness.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Now walk four steps to the door and come back. Slowly.
[SEG0031] person_3 (PATIENT): Ok. Ah, it is paining. But I can, see, one, two, three, four.

[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. So Ottawa rules, there is malleolar zone pain, but no bony tenderness on the posterior edges, and you managed four steps here. So I am not sending you for an x-ray today.
[SEG0033] person_3 (PATIENT): Means no fracture, doctor? I was thinking the bone itself is gone.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): I think it is a lateral ligament sprain, not a broken bone. If the swelling increases or you cannot walk, then we will do the x-ray.
[SEG0035] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He has selection trials next week, doctor. Can we not do the x-ray today itself, to be safe?
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): No, not indicated today. You rest the ankle, keep it elevated on two pillows, ice fifteen minutes three times in the day. No cricket till this settles.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): For the pain I will prescribe paracetamol, 500 mg, one tablet by mouth, three times a day after food, for five days.
[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): Ok. And metformine I continue, no? That one I know, 500 morning and night.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, continue your usual tablets. Sorry, the screen blinked. The sugar one is 500 twice, yes, I heard you.
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): The others I don't know, doctor. Amlodipine I don't know the mg. Cholesterol name also I don't know.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): If it is not better in one week, come back and see me.
[SEG0042] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Traffic was bad also today, we started very early from the house. We will come if needed. Thank you, doctor.
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. I will do the ice and keep the leg up.

spec.situation: Young player who twisted the ankle yesterday; swelling, can bear weight with pain; doctor applies Ottawa rules aloud, no X-ray unless it worsens; rest and elevation advice.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

omissions.text: Patient reported he can bear weight/walk on the right ankle, though it hurts and there may be a small limp; this functional symptom detail was said before and during the exam.
Mechanism of injury: while fielding cricket, his foot went inwards on a rough patch, causing an inversion-type twist.
No pop sound was noticed at the time of injury; patient said he did not notice any pop.
Diabetes/sugar is an ongoing past medical condition, inferred from current metformin use and discussion of 'sugar tablets', but it is not recorded in past medical history.
Paracetamol was instructed to be taken after food; this administration instruction is missing from the recorded medication/plan.
